title: 2 Corinthians Chapter 13 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Corinthians chapter 13 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Corinthians Chapter 13 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Corinthians Chapter 13.

questions.question: In 2 Corinthians 13, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The mouth of two or three witnesses
questions.correctAnswer: The mouth of two or three witnesses
questions.explanation: This is found in 2 Corinthians 13:1, which states that in the mouth of two or three witnesses shall every word be established.

questions.question: How many times does Paul mention he is coming to them?
questions.explanation: Paul states in 2 Corinthians 13:1 that this is the third time he is coming to them.

questions.question: What does Paul say will not happen if he comes again?
questions.explanation: In 2 Corinthians 13:2, Paul says that if he comes again, he will not spare those who have sinned.

questions.question: What proof is being sought by the Corinthians?
options: Proof of Christ speaking in Paul
questions.correctAnswer: Proof of Christ speaking in Paul
questions.explanation: According to 2 Corinthians 13:3, they seek a proof of Christ speaking in Paul.

questions.question: How does Paul describe Christ in relation to weakness and power?
questions.explanation: This is stated in 2 Corinthians 13:4, where Paul explains that Christ was crucified through weakness but lives by the power of God.

questions.question: What are believers encouraged to examine?
questions.explanation: In 2 Corinthians 13:5, Paul urges them to examine themselves to see if they are in the faith.

questions.question: What does Paul say about those who may be reprobates?
questions.explanation: Paul mentions in 2 Corinthians 13:5 that if they do not know Jesus Christ is in them, they may be reprobates.

questions.question: What does Paul foretell in 2 Corinthians 13:2?
questions.explanation: Paul states in 2 Corinthians 13:2 that he forewarns them, indicating he will come again.

questions.question: What is the significance of two or three witnesses according to Paul?
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 13:1 indicates that in the mouth of two or three witnesses every word shall be established, implying the importance of multiple attestations.

questions.question: According to 2 Corinthians 13:4, how do believers also relate to Christ's power?
options: We are weak but will live with him
questions.correctAnswer: We are weak but will live with him
questions.explanation: Paul states in 2 Corinthians 13:4 that although they are weak in Him, they shall live with Him by the power of God.

questions.question: What does Paul claim about his presence among them when he is absent?
questions.explanation: In 2 Corinthians 13:3, Paul emphasizes that he is not weak but mighty in them, even when absent.

questions.question: Is it true that Paul warned the Corinthians about those who have sinned?
questions.explanation: In 2 Corinthians 13:2, Paul explicitly mentions he writes to those who have sinned.

questions.question: Is it true that believers are encouraged to prove their own selves?
questions.explanation: Paul encourages them to prove their own selves in 2 Corinthians 13:5.

questions.question: Is it false that Christ was never weak according to Paul?
questions.explanation: Paul states in 2 Corinthians 13:4 that Christ was crucified through weakness.

questions.question: Is it false that Paul has never visited the Corinthians?
questions.explanation: Paul mentions he is coming to them for the third time in 2 Corinthians 13:1, indicating he has visited before.

medium.title: 2 Corinthians Chapter 13 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Corinthians Chapter 13 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What does Paul express confidence in regarding the Corinthians in 2 Corinthians 13:6?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Paul states, 'But I trust that ye shall know that we are not reprobates.' (2 Corinthians 13:6)

questions.question: What does 2 Corinthians 13:7 encourage the Corinthians to do?
questions.explanation: This answer aligns with the text, which says, 'Now I pray to God that ye do no evil...but that ye should do that which is honest...' (2 Corinthians 13:7)

questions.question: According to 2 Corinthians 13:8, what can we do regarding the truth?
questions.explanation: This is correct as it states, 'For we can do nothing against the truth, but for the truth.' (2 Corinthians 13:8)

questions.question: What does 2 Corinthians 13:9 express about Paul’s feelings towards the Corinthians' strength?
questions.explanation: This is correct because it states, 'For we are glad, when we are weak, and ye are strong...' (2 Corinthians 13:9)

questions.question: According to 2 Corinthians 13:10, why does Paul write these things while absent?
questions.explanation: This is correct because he says, '...to edification, and not to destruction.' (2 Corinthians 13:10)

questions.question: What does 2 Corinthians 13:1 indicate is necessary for establishing every word?
questions.explanation: This is correct as it states, 'In the mouth of two or three witnesses shall every word be established.' (2 Corinthians 13:1)

questions.question: In 2 Corinthians 13:3, what does Paul seek proof of?
questions.explanation: This is correct as he states, 'Since ye seek a proof of Christ speaking in me...' (2 Corinthians 13:3)

questions.question: What does 2 Corinthians 13:4 say about Jesus Christ's power?
options: He lives by the power of God
questions.correctAnswer: He lives by the power of God
questions.explanation: This is correct because it says, '...yet he liveth by the power of God.' (2 Corinthians 13:4)

questions.question: What does 2 Corinthians 13:5 encourage believers to do?
questions.explanation: This is correct as it states, 'Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith...' (2 Corinthians 13:5)

questions.question: In the context of 2 Corinthians 13:6 and 13:7, what should be the focus of the Corinthians' actions?
questions.explanation: This is correct as it infers that they should focus on doing honest actions rather than seeking approval. (2 Corinthians 13:6-7)

questions.question: In light of 2 Corinthians 13:8 and 13:9, what should believers prioritize in their lives?
questions.explanation: This is correct because it emphasizes doing nothing against the truth and being glad in weakness while being strong in the truth. (2 Corinthians 13:8-9)

questions.question: According to 2 Corinthians 13:10, what does Paul desire for his ministry?
questions.explanation: This is correct as he mentions that he desires to use the power given for edification, not destruction. (2 Corinthians 13:10)

questions.question: True or False: Paul trusts that the Corinthians will recognize their strength in Christ.
questions.explanation: This is true as Paul expresses trust in their understanding and recognition of faith. (2 Corinthians 13:6)

questions.question: True or False: The power of God is shown through weakness according to 2 Corinthians.
questions.explanation: This is false; while weakness is noted, it is the power of God that ultimately gives strength, not weakness itself. (2 Corinthians 13:4)

questions.question: True or False: Paul was concerned about his reputation more than the truth.
questions.explanation: This is false as Paul emphasizes the truth over personal appearance or reputation. (2 Corinthians 13:7-8)

hard.title: 2 Corinthians Chapter 13 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Corinthians Chapter 13.

questions.question: What does Paul encourage the brethren to be in 2 Corinthians 13:11?
questions.explanation: Paul encourages the brethren to 'be perfect' as part of his farewell, emphasizing the need for spiritual maturity and completeness. (2 Corinthians 13:11)

questions.question: What greeting does Paul instruct in 2 Corinthians 13:12?
questions.explanation: Paul instructs the Corinthians to greet one another with 'an holy kiss', which reflects the cultural practice of expressing love and unity among believers. (2 Corinthians 13:12)

questions.question: What does Paul mention in 2 Corinthians 13:13 regarding the saints?
questions.explanation: Paul conveys that 'all the saints salute you', indicating a collective support and greeting from believers, which fosters unity in the faith. (2 Corinthians 13:13)

questions.question: What three elements does Paul mention in his benediction in 2 Corinthians 13:14?
questions.explanation: In his benediction, Paul mentions 'the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the communion of the Holy Ghost', summarizing the relationship among the Trinity and their role in the believers' lives. (2 Corinthians 13:14)

questions.question: What does Paul mean by 'be of one mind' in 2 Corinthians 13:11?
questions.explanation: 'Be of one mind' indicates a call for unity and shared purpose among the believers, reflecting the importance of harmony in the body of Christ. (2 Corinthians 13:11)

questions.question: What is the significance of the phrase 'God of love and peace' in 2 Corinthians 13:11?
questions.explanation: The 'God of love and peace' signifies that God's nature is fundamentally linked to love and peace, reassuring believers of His presence and character. (2 Corinthians 13:11)

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'koinonia' in 2 Corinthians 13:14 mean?
questions.explanation: 'Koinonia' is the Greek word used for 'communion' in this context, meaning fellowship or partnership, emphasizing the relational aspect of believers with the Holy Spirit. (2 Corinthians 13:14)

questions.question: Which literary device is used in 2 Corinthians 13:14 when Paul lists three elements?
questions.explanation: The use of three elements ('grace, love, communion') in Paul's benediction is an example of tricolon, which emphasizes the completeness of the blessings he wishes for the believers. (2 Corinthians 13:14)

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage connects to the theme of peace mentioned in 2 Corinthians 13:11?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26:3 speaks of God keeping in perfect peace those whose minds are steadfast, echoing the theme of peace found in 2 Corinthians 13:11. (2 Corinthians 13:11)

questions.question: Which other New Testament passage reflects the call for unity found in 2 Corinthians 13:11?
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:2 encourages believers to be like-minded and have the same love, reflecting the call for unity in 2 Corinthians 13:11. (2 Corinthians 13:11)

questions.question: What comes immediately before Paul’s farewell in 2 Corinthians 13:11?
questions.explanation: The phrase 'Finally, brethren' introduces Paul's farewell, indicating that he is summarizing his thoughts and concluding the letter. (2 Corinthians 13:11)

questions.question: What does Paul express regarding his feelings towards weakness in 2 Corinthians 13:9?
questions.explanation: Paul expresses that he is glad when he is weak, as it highlights the strength of Christ working through him, which aligns with the theme of relying on God's power. (2 Corinthians 13:9)

questions.question: In 2 Corinthians 13, Paul mentions the need for what kind of examination?
questions.explanation: Paul instructs the Corinthians to 'examine yourselves', emphasizing the importance of personal reflection on one's faith and relationship with Christ. (2 Corinthians 13:5)

questions.question: True or False: Paul instructs believers to greet one another with a holy kiss in 2 Corinthians 13:12.
questions.explanation: Paul indeed instructs believers to greet one another with a holy kiss as a sign of love and unity among fellow Christians. (2 Corinthians 13:12)

questions.question: True or False: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ is mentioned as part of the closing in 2 Corinthians 13:14.
questions.explanation: This statement is false as it is indeed mentioned; the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ is part of Paul's closing in 2 Corinthians 13:14, alongside the love of God and the communion of the Holy Ghost.

theological.title: 2 Corinthians Chapter 13 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Corinthians Chapter 13 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Corinthians 13:4 teach about the nature of Christ's crucifixion and resurrection?
options: Christ was crucified through weakness but lives by the power of God
Christ's resurrection is purely symbolic and not actual
Christ's power was diminished by His crucifixion
Christ's resurrection depends on human works
questions.correctAnswer: Christ was crucified through weakness but lives by the power of God
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 13:4 states that although Christ was crucified through weakness, He lives by the power of God, affirming the doctrine of Christ's real death and resurrection with divine power.

questions.question: What doctrine about sanctification does 2 Corinthians 13:5 teach regarding self-examination?
options: Believers must examine themselves to verify that Christ dwells in them
Sanctification is a one-time event with no need for self-examination
Self-examination is unnecessary because faith is guaranteed
Only church leaders should examine faith, not individual believers
questions.correctAnswer: Believers must examine themselves to verify that Christ dwells in them
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 13:5 instructs believers to examine themselves to see whether they are in the faith and to know if Jesus Christ is in them, emphasizing ongoing self-examination in sanctification.

questions.question: What doctrine about apostolic authority is taught in 2 Corinthians 13:10?
options: Paul writes with authority to build up the church, not to destroy
Paul uses his authority primarily to condemn and exclude
Apostolic authority is based on popular approval
Paul’s authority is only valid when he is physically present
questions.correctAnswer: Paul writes with authority to build up the church, not to destroy
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 13:10 reveals that Paul uses his authority, given by the Lord, for edification and not destruction, affirming the constructive purpose of apostolic discipline.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Corinthians 13:14 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 13:14 invokes the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, the love of God, and the communion of the Holy Ghost together, highlighting the unity and distinct persons of the Trinity.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is emphasized in 2 Corinthians 13:8 when Paul states, 'we can do nothing against the truth, but for the truth'?
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 13:8 emphasizes God's faithfulness and the commitment of Paul and the apostles to uphold truth, showing their alignment with God's unchanging truth.

questions.question: How does 2 Corinthians 13:11 connect with the broader biblical theme of Christian community?
options: It commands believers to pursue unity and peace, reflecting the New Testament call to communal harmony
It replaces Old Testament purity laws with new social codes
It encourages isolation to avoid conflict
questions.correctAnswer: It commands believers to pursue unity and peace, reflecting the New Testament call to communal harmony
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 13:11 exhorts believers to be of one mind and live in peace, which aligns with New Testament teachings about the unity of the body of Christ (e.g., Ephesians 4:3).

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection is fulfilled by the phrase 'in the mouth of two or three witnesses shall every word be established' in 2 Corinthians 13:1?
options: It echoes Old Testament judicial standards, affirming apostolic authority and accountability
It alludes to pagan legal codes
It contradicts New Testament grace teachings
It introduces a new standard unrelated to Scripture
questions.correctAnswer: It echoes Old Testament judicial standards, affirming apostolic authority and accountability
questions.explanation: The phrase in 2 Corinthians 13:1 cites Deuteronomy 19:15, showing continuity in biblical law regarding the establishment of truth and supporting apostolic authority.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 2 Corinthians 13:2 and 13:10 teach about apostolic discipline and authority?
options: Paul warns of exercising discipline with severity, but with the goal of edification
Paul forbids any discipline to avoid conflict
Paul only disciplines when present physically
Discipline is to be used for destruction, not restoration
questions.correctAnswer: Paul warns of exercising discipline with severity, but with the goal of edification
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 13:2 warns that Paul will not spare sinners on his next visit, while 13:10 clarifies that his authority is for building up, showing discipline is severe but redemptive.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about Christian weakness and strength is taught in 2 Corinthians 13:4 and 13:9?
options: Christ’s power is perfected in weakness, and the church prays for mutual strength and maturity
Weakness is shameful and to be avoided at all costs
Strength comes only through human effort
Christ’s power is unrelated to human weakness
questions.correctAnswer: Christ’s power is perfected in weakness, and the church prays for mutual strength and maturity
questions.explanation: Verse 4 explains Christ’s resurrection power amid weakness; verse 9 expresses gladness in weakness when others are strong, both teaching dependence on divine strength.

questions.question: What synthesis do 2 Corinthians 13:5 and 13:6 teach about the assurance of salvation and apostolic integrity?
options: Believers must self-examine to confirm faith, and Paul trusts that he and his co-workers are not rejected by God
Salvation assurance is impossible and Paul doubts his own ministry
Self-examination is unnecessary because Paul guarantees salvation
Apostles need no self-examination or assurance
questions.correctAnswer: Believers must self-examine to confirm faith, and Paul trusts that he and his co-workers are not rejected by God
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 13:5 calls for self-examination of faith; 13:6 expresses Paul’s confidence that he is not disqualified, showing the balance of personal and apostolic assurance.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that 2 Corinthians 13:2–3 teaches that Paul threatens harsh judgment without basis. What does this passage actually teach?
options: Paul warns of judgment based on prior sins and the authority of Christ speaking through him
Paul arbitrarily threatens punishment regardless of repentance
Paul's threats are only rhetorical and have no practical consequence
Paul defers all judgment to human leaders rather than divine authority
questions.correctAnswer: Paul warns of judgment based on prior sins and the authority of Christ speaking through him
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 13:2–3 explains Paul’s warning comes from Christ’s authority and previous sins committed, indicating a serious but justified disciplinary stance.

questions.question: What doctrine about Christian fellowship and peace is taught in 2 Corinthians 13:11?
options: Believers are called to be perfect, united in mind, and to live in peace, reflecting God's nature
Christian fellowship is optional and unrelated to sanctification
Peace is a worldly ideal, not a Christian mandate
Perfection is impossible and not commanded
questions.correctAnswer: Believers are called to be perfect, united in mind, and to live in peace, reflecting God's nature
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 13:11 exhorts believers to unity and peace, highlighting sanctification as communal and reflecting the God of love and peace.

questions.question: What attribute of God is especially demonstrated by the prayer in 2 Corinthians 13:7, where Paul asks that the Corinthians do no evil?
questions.explanation: Paul’s prayer in 2 Corinthians 13:7 for the Corinthians to do what is honest, even if he and his companions are considered disqualified, shows God’s patience and longsuffering in dealing with sinners.

questions.question: How do 2 Corinthians 13:12 and 13:13 together reflect the theological significance of holy fellowship among believers?
options: They show the importance of mutual greeting as an expression of sanctified communal love
They impose legalistic rules on social interaction
They emphasize formal hierarchy over fellowship
They discourage physical expressions of community
questions.correctAnswer: They show the importance of mutual greeting as an expression of sanctified communal love
questions.explanation: Verse 12 commands greeting one another with a holy kiss, and verse 13 extends greetings from all saints, emphasizing holy fellowship and mutual love among believers.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about Christ's presence and power is taught in 2 Corinthians 13:3 and 13:4?
options: Christ’s power is mighty in believers despite apparent weakness, evidenced by His resurrection
Christ’s presence is limited and weak in believers
Believers receive power only through their own efforts
questions.correctAnswer: Christ’s power is mighty in believers despite apparent weakness, evidenced by His resurrection
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 13:3 speaks of Christ's mighty power in believers, and 13:4 explains Christ was crucified through weakness but lives by God's power, teaching divine strength in weakness.
